transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — jamal, priya, liam, great to meet you. We'll give a 30-40 minute walkthrough of our hosted search pipeline: embeddings + reranker, then leave time for q&a. Miguel will demo the rerank flow.
[00:22] Jamal (Customer): Thanks Ava. We're really trying to improve recall and relevance for product search; current relevance is noisy, lots of synonyms missing. Our infra team is sensitive to latency and cost obviously.
[00:45] Miguel (Redwood SE): Great — quick agenda: 1) show Console + routes; 2) call the embeddings endpoint with a small sample; 3) show retrieval + rerank end-to-end; 4) discuss performance tuning and security.
[01:10] Priya (Customer): Quick Q — is this hosted only? We have a mix of public SaaS and a few regulated tenants.
[01:30] Ava: We support Hosted API (fastest to start), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem). For initial POC hosted is easiest. If you need data isolation we can move to Dedicated.
[01:50] Liam: For hosted, how do you handle data residency and KMS? We have encryption requirements.
[02:05] Miguel: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations, and we have region pinning for residency. We can provide audit logs and longer retention in enterprise packages. There will be a security docs link after the call.
[02:30] Ava: OK Miguel, demo time.
[02:45] Miguel: I'm in the Console — here are routes, model catalog, and an "embeddings" route we created for this account: note the model version pinning. I'll show a live call against the embeddings endpoint using a small product title set.
[03:12] [03:12] Miguel: (typing) Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":"running shoes blue"}' — response comes back with a 1536-d vector. In hosted we return vectors quickly; in our demo tenant p95 was around 120ms for embeddings but your numbers will vary with sequence length and batching.
[04:05] Priya: That p95 seems high — what about parallelism?
[04:18] Miguel: For embeddings we recommend batching client-side for throughput. We also include automatic caching (prefix and KV-like caches) inside the runtime for repeated doc indexing patterns — that cuts costs for index-time generation. For real-time low-latency you can use smaller models or dedicated pools.
[04:45] Jamal: Walk me through the rerank call — is that a separate endpoint?
[05:10] Miguel: Yes, two-step flow: 1) Search retrieval (vector similarity) using embeddings; 2) Send top-N candidates to the reranker endpoint which scores using a cross-encoder. In our Console you can create a pipeline route that wires retrieval -> rerank. The reranker endpoint accepts context + query and returns ranked candidate ids and scores.
[05:52] [05:52] Miguel: (shows code) Example: POST /v1/rerank {"model":"rerank-large","query":"waterproof hiking boots","candidates":[{id:1, text:"..."}, ...]} -> returns an ordered list with scores.
[06:25] Priya: How do you avoid double-embedding costs? If we embed docs at index-time and also embed query on each request...
[06:40] Miguel: Good question. Common pattern: precompute and store doc vectors (you pay once), compute query vector at request time. Retrieval is a cheap nearest neighbor op. If you use the two-step rerank with cross-encoder we only encode the candidates (not full corpus) so it's efficient. Also prefix/KV cache helps when queries are similar.
[07:05] Ava: Also note Optimize suggestions in Console — it will recommend batching sizes and quantization profiles based on your workload to balance latency and token-cost.
[07:30] Jamal: Can you show the Console analytics for a route?
[07:40] Miguel: Sure — here is the route dashboard: per-route latency, token breakdown (prompt vs completion), and cost-per-1k tokens. You can set SLO alerts and also do canary rollouts to test a new model version for a slice of traffic.
[08:12] [08:12] Priya: For the reranker cross-encoder model, what's the expected token latency? We are aiming for p95 end-to-end <400ms for search.
[08:30] Miguel: P95 depends on model size and topN. For hosted customers using rerank-large with top10 we often see end-to-end p95 around 350-700ms depending on load. Dedicated pools can get that lower. We'll scope this for your 50k docs dataset.
[09:00] Jamal: Cost ballpark? Monthly for ~1M queries and 50k docs?
[09:15] Ava: We'll send a pricing spreadsheet, but ballpark hosted costs for two-step retrieval + rerank (open models) are usually dominated by rerank compute. Optimize can suggest quantized reranker or smaller cross-encoders to reduce cost while measuring quality delta.
[09:40] [09:40] Liam: Any throttling or rate-limits we should know about for hosted?
[09:50] Miguel: Default quotas applied per account, you can request rate increases; Dedicated gives you guaranteed throughput. In Console you can also configure burst policies.
[10:20] Priya: We use Elasticsearch for initial retrieval today. How do people typically migrate?
[10:35] Miguel: Commonly teams keep ES for bag-of-words and add vector retrieval as a parallel pipeline for semantic layers. For a full migration we provide sample ingest scripts and embeddings generation steps. We'll share a notebook for your engineers.
[11:05] Ava: Quick pause — real customer note: we recently helped a retail customer reduce false positives by doing a two‑stage rerank and feature-tuning the cross-encoder.
[11:32] Jamal: Awesome. Can we test with our sample dataset?
[11:40] Ava: Yep — for a hosted POC we can ingest 50k docs. Typical POC plan: 1) ingest & index docs; 2) run baseline retrieval + rerank; 3) evaluate with your labeled queries; 4) iterate model config. We'll scope time and success metrics on the scoping call.
[12:05] [12:05] Miguel: Now demoing a live rerank call — sending top5 candidates for a sample query. (typing) Response back: candidates reordered, includes per-candidate score and debug tokens. Note: some debug keys are verbose in this demo tenant.
[12:40] Priya: The debug payload is helpful. Does Console store these for privacy reasons?
[12:50] Miguel: By default we keep short-term traces for debugging; enterprise customers can opt into minimal logging and full audit logs via S3 export or their own SIEM.
[13:15] Jamal: Security checklist — SOC2, SAML, RBAC?
[13:28] Ava: We have a SOC2 Type II report, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC in Console, and customer-managed KMS. We'll attach our security pack.
[13:50] Liam: Network egress concerns — can we run in a VPC?
[14:02] Miguel: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and can be deployed on-prem for air-gapped setups. For hosted we also support private endpoints and region pinning to minimize egress.
[14:30] [14:30] Priya: How do you measure quality regressions? We need evals tied to prompt sets.
[14:45] Ava: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts. You can upload evaluation sets; it will track metrics per model version and create alerts when delta exceeds thresholds.
[15:05] Miguel: Also you'll get cost vs quality tradeoff dashboards so you can see the impact of quantization or switching to a smaller reranker.
[15:30] Jamal: Any gotchas about indexing PDFs and long descriptions?
[15:45] Miguel: For long docs we chunk, embed each chunk and store mapping back to original doc. Sequence length affects embedding latency and vector size sometimes. For long-context reranking we use cross-encoders with truncation heuristics and also support structured output in the rerank payloads.
[16:10] [16:10] Ava: Quick product note: we have an embeddings-only hosted route for async indexing jobs which is cheaper for bulk ingestion.
[16:30] Priya: If we run POC, what's the expected timeline?
[16:40] Ava: Typical hosted POC is 2-3 weeks: ingest + baseline run (1 week), iterate (1 week), final evaluation (a few days). If you want deeper integration or dedicated capacity that's a longer procurement path.
[17:05] Jamal: We care about maintainability — how often do you push new model versions?
[17:20] Miguel: We publish model catalog updates regularly; Console lets you pin model versions per route and do canaries for rollouts. For production you control when to adopt new versions.
[17:45] [17:45] Priya: Could you show the Postman/SDK snippets for rerank?
[17:55] Miguel: (shares screen) Here's an SDK snippet in Python and Node; payload includes candidates array and optional metadata per-candidate. We'll upload these to the shared Git repo after the call.
[18:20] Ava: Recap for next steps: we'll send pricing, security docs, and example payloads. Customer to provide dataset and success criteria. Then schedule POC scoping.
[18:40] Jamal: Sounds good. A couple small questions — can you support per-customer rate limits and per-route logging?
[18:55] Miguel: Yes to both; Console has per-route logging toggles and we support per-account quotas.
[19:20] Priya: One more on cost: do you provide token-level cost attribution?
[19:30] Ava: Yes, Console shows token-level breakdown and cost attribution per route and per model, which helped a customer uncover a hidden cost in XL cross-encoder usage.
[19:50] [19:50] Liam: Anything else from your side?
[19:58] Ava: No, thanks. We'll follow up by sending the collateral.
[20:10] [20:10] Jamal: Thank you, appreciate the demo.
[47:58] [47:58] (call end)
